question: How do the server, the page and the desktop shell fit together?
tldr: One Node server per project; page and desktop shell just talk to it.
answer: The server owns files, git, the index, terminals and the chat, and pushes changes over an event stream. The Svelte page renders them; the Rust window only starts servers and hosts the page.
why: Three processes and several channels (HTTP, events, WebSockets) are not obvious from the files.

nodes.label: Desktop shell
nodes.tldr: GTK window, one server per project
nodes.explain: Starts a server on a free port per project, shows the page in WebKitGTK and stops them on close.

nodes.label: Svelte page
nodes.explain: The UI built by Vite; state lives in one reactive store fed by the event stream.

nodes.label: Node server
nodes.tldr: Owns the project's data and agents
nodes.explain: Serves the page, a JSON API, an events stream and WebSockets for terminals and language servers.

nodes.label: Code index
nodes.explain: rust-analyzer or scip-clang output turned into modules and items that diagram links name.

nodes.label: Agent chat
nodes.explain: Runs Claude Code with the user's login and streams items to the page.

nodes.label: Terminals
nodes.explain: Shells whose commands, folder and exit codes are tracked, attached over WebSocket.

nodes.label: Project folder and git
nodes.explain: The working tree the agent edits and the server watches.

nodes.label: Claude Code login
nodes.explain: Cockpit uses it through the SDK; no API key.
